mcq.q: The price of a good rises from ₹10 to ₹12, and the quantity supplied rises from 100 to 130 units. Price elasticity of supply (percentage method) is:
mcq.explain: Elasticity of supply = % change in quantity supplied ÷ % change in price = (30 ÷ 100) ÷ (2 ÷ 10) = 30% ÷ 20% = 1.5. Supply is relatively elastic here: producers increase output more than proportionately to the rise in price.

mcq.q: Price rises from ₹8 to ₹12 and quantity supplied rises from 40 to 60 units. Arc elasticity of supply is:
mcq.explain: Arc elasticity of supply = [ΔQ ÷ (Q1 + Q2)] × [(P1 + P2) ÷ ΔP] = (20 ÷ 100) × (20 ÷ 4) = 0.2 × 5 = 1. Supply is unit elastic over this range. Using the original values alone would give (20/40) ÷ (4/8) = 1 as well in this special case, because price and quantity rise by the same proportion.

mcq.q: For the supply function Qs = −20 + 4P, the point elasticity of supply at P = ₹10 is:
mcq.explain: At P = 10, Qs = −20 + 40 = 20. Point elasticity of supply = (dQ/dP) × (P/Q) = 4 × 10/20 = 2. A linear supply curve that cuts the price axis at a positive price (here at P = 5) has elasticity greater than one at every point.

mcq.q: A straight-line supply curve that passes through the origin has a price elasticity of supply:
options: Greater than one at every point
Equal to one at every point
Less than one at every point
Equal to zero
mcq.explain: For any straight-line supply curve passing through the origin, P/Q equals the inverse of the slope, so elasticity = (dQ/dP) × (P/Q) = 1 at every point, whatever the slope. A line cutting the price axis has elasticity above one, and a line cutting the quantity axis has elasticity below one.
mcq.fast: Through origin = 1; cuts price axis = > 1; cuts quantity axis = < 1.

mcq.q: A government subsidy to producers of a good will:
options: Shift the supply curve to the right (increase in supply)
Cause a movement along the supply curve
Shift the supply curve to the left
Leave supply unchanged
mcq.explain: A subsidy reduces the producers' cost per unit, so they are willing to supply more at every price. This is an increase in supply, shown by a rightward shift of the whole supply curve. A tax on production raises costs and shifts supply to the left. Only a change in the good's own price causes a movement along the curve.
mcq.topic: Movement along vs shift of the supply curve
mcq.fast: Cost down (subsidy, better technology) = supply shifts right.

mcq.q: Which of the following will cause a decrease in the supply of wheat?
options: A fall in the price of wheat
Improvement in seed technology
A rise in the prices of fertilisers and diesel
A subsidy on irrigation
mcq.explain: A rise in input prices raises the cost of production, so farmers supply less wheat at every price — a decrease in supply, shown by a leftward shift. A fall in the price of wheat itself causes a contraction along the curve, not a decrease in supply. Better technology and subsidies increase supply.
mcq.fast: Decrease in supply = non-price factor raising cost. Own-price fall = contraction.

mcq.q: The supply of a perishable commodity like fresh fish brought to the market on a given day is, for that day:
options: Perfectly inelastic
Perfectly elastic
Unit elastic
Highly elastic
mcq.explain: In the very short period (market period), the quantity of a perishable good like fresh fish is fixed and must be sold that day whatever the price. Supply cannot respond to price changes, so it is perfectly inelastic and the supply curve is vertical. Over longer periods, supply becomes more elastic.
mcq.topic: Elasticity of supply: meaning and types
mcq.fast: Very short period + perishable = vertical supply.

mcq.q: Supply of a good is generally more elastic:
options: In the short run than in the long run
When production needs a long time to adjust
When the good is highly perishable
In the long run than in the short run
mcq.explain: Elasticity of supply depends on how easily producers can change output. In the long run firms can expand plants, new firms can enter and resources can be moved, so supply responds more to price changes. In the short run, fixed capacity limits the response. Long production periods and perishability make supply less elastic.

mcq.q: The law of supply states that, other things remaining the same:
options: Quantity supplied varies inversely with price
Supply creates its own demand
Quantity supplied varies directly with price
Supply is always perfectly elastic
mcq.explain: The law of supply states that, other things remaining constant, the quantity supplied of a good rises when its price rises and falls when its price falls, a direct or positive relationship. That is why the supply curve normally slopes upward. "Supply creates its own demand" is Say's law of markets, which is a different idea.
mcq.topic: The law of supply: schedule and curve
mcq.fast: Supply: price and quantity move together (direct).
